text_en: The square has been loud with orders for days. Now the loudest order is where to put a chair.
Not there. The leg will catch in the drain.
Then we put the short people at that end. They will not notice.
They will notice falling over.
A table that applauds when you sit down. Very festive.
I have brought a contribution.
Is it meant to be making that noise?
That is a cooking noise.
We will discover what it is called when it reaches a bowl.
A helper carries a stack of bowls past them. Everyone steps aside at a different speed.
If you have a free hand, there is work for it. If you have two, I will be delighted.
These boards need bracing before anyone puts hot food on them.
There are serving things waiting at the storehouse. I know the turn with the least mud.
And the last verse needs room for names of every length.
You cannot all have the same pair of hands.
You do not have to. Choose two jobs. We will finish the other together.
Nobody misses supper because we liked a different errand.
Good. I like a map with more than one useful road.
Wood first. A clear place for the bowls makes the rest easier.
Then we bring the bowls. Excellent division of worrying.
I will borrow other voices for the verse.
We start at the storehouse. Nothing heavy through the market steps.
Then we make room in the song for the people carrying it.
I will find someone who can hold the other end of a board.
Song first. It is harder to find a name once everyone has a mouthful.
Then the tables. It is harder to hold a bowl once everyone is on the ground.
I will make sure the serving things find us.
Hold it there. No, lower. I need the board level, not impressed.
Will it hold that many people?
It will hold the dishes. The people get chairs.
I was looking forward to standing on it.
You can disappoint yourself before the soup does it for you.
The helper laughs and stops gripping the board hard enough to shake it.
There. You can let go of that end. I have this one.
Is that your best table-making voice?
It is my voice for people putting their fingers where the hammer goes.
Some chairs were borrowed from kitchens. One was borrowed from somewhere that owned no other furniture.
We could hide that one at the end.
We could fix it.
I like that answer. The end keeps getting all the interesting chairs.
Put your foot on the pad while I fit it. Not on my hand.
There. It does not rock now.
Leave it near the middle. Someone should get to sit close without feeling borrowed.
It is a chair. It does not ask who brought it.
She puts it where the light reaches the seat.
This gap stays open.
For the food?
For whoever carries it. And whoever cannot step over three people to sit down.
A very considerate gap.
Do not sing at it. It is already doing its job.
A helper sets the last bowl down. The table does not move.
You can hear the difference.
I prefer the part you cannot hear.
Not the steps. A short route becomes a long route when the soup goes down it first.
The soup is not leaving my hands.
Then you have a very good reason to avoid the steps.
The bowls are fragile.
So we carry them low and stop at the turn. I will see who is coming the other way.
You make fetching bowls sound like a heroic expedition.
Everything sounds heroic until somebody asks how many bowls came back.
Nixie moves the heaviest bundle to the hand closest to the wall.
I can take the last stack too.
Wait. Take a breath first.
Everyone else is moving.
Then they can keep moving around us.
I have a free hand. The pot only needs one until someone starts criticizing it.
I will save my criticism for the square.
The stack changes hands without a bowl being dropped.
There. Faster without pretending it was lighter.
I thought you would tell me to hurry.
I know where we are going. We can get there with all the bowls.
If we need another load, can you show the next pair of hands where we went?
You are making them lead the way back?
They know the steps now. I do not have to carry every bowl to know it will arrive.
That sounds like a holiday.
Only if nobody asks me to carry the tables.
She hands over the empty sling and follows while the helper chooses the turn.
This way.
Good. It is not only my route now.
Short names, long names, names that need a second breath. There is room.
Mine will spoil the rhythm.
Then the rhythm can improve itself.
A sensible rhythm. We should invite it more often.
Could I bring my mother's name instead?
If that is the name you wish us to sing.
Pippa leaves a space before writing. The guest says it once, then again slowly.
Like that?
Like that.
I can give you a name. I would rather not give you the story.
I asked for one line. I did not ask for every page.
We can keep a seat where you do not have to face the square.
I might join the song. Later.
Then later is a perfectly good time for it.
Pippa rehearses the syllables softly enough that only the guest can correct them.
You changed the tune.
The name was doing nothing wrong.
Once together. You may miss the note, but do not lose the person beside you.
I have already missed three notes.
A vigorous beginning.
Will the song still work?
It is a song, Kera. The point is that we are singing it.
Good. I was worried it needed a bottle.
The refrain wanders off-key, finds another voice, and comes back changed.
Keep that part.
Stop at the storehouse door. The lane beyond it is not clear.
Leave the serving things inside. Nobody carries them through a fight.
The square can keep setting places. We will clear this turn.
The ones in front are moving when that bellbound corpse does.
And one behind them is reaching past. Read both before we commit.
We can hold the front and choose our opening.
No hurry that costs someone the road back.
The load stays on dry boards. The group steps into the lane with empty hands ready for weapons.
The last stack is here.
Set it on the brace. Not the edge.
The helper can show the way back if anyone needs another load.
And the verse has enough room for the new arrivals.
Then sit before somebody finds you another useful thing to do.
My contribution first.
That depends on what it is doing now.
Kera lifts the lid with the seriousness of someone presenting a thesis.
Rule of the Harvest Supper: one dish, one name. You say the name, you get a bowl.
I brought a dish. It is technically soup.
It is moving.
It is effervescent.
I will eat it! For the festival!
Nixie ate it. Nixie was fine. Nixie glowed faintly for an hour.
It was very memorable.
That is not an accepted tasting category.
It is now.
We can put it in the program. Soup: memorable. Tables: upright.
The helper passes the next bowl. For once, no one tells them to hurry.
There is ordinary bread if you need something with fewer opinions.
I can support both kinds of food.
A scientifically fair response.
After Crownfall, travelers stopped paying. So we stopped charging. Twice a day, a meal, no coin.
That is generous.
It is practical. A fed traveler says their name at the door. A hungry one slips past the register.
So the meal is a count.
The meal is a meal, knight. The count is a bonus.
I can say a name. I do not think I can sing it in front of everyone.
Speaking is allowed to remain speaking.
This seat is steady.
That is Jori's highest recommendation.
You can sit before deciding how loud to be.
There is room to pass behind the chair.
The guest touches the back of the chair, then looks toward the open square.
We are comparing the chairs. You can help us settle the matter.
There is no matter. They are all chairs.
That is one side of the argument.
This one is a very good chair.
A decisive answer.
I will sit here for a moment.
You do not have to.
I know. I would like to.
I will bring the bread within reach.
The guest sits. The silence does not ask them to fill it.
Are you still arguing about the chairs?
We have moved on to bowls.
There is still no argument.
Stay here if you like. The song starts from wherever you are standing.
The guest stays close enough to hear a familiar voice.
I thought I might listen from here.
It is a good place to listen.
Nobody needs to move closer.
If you want to join, you will hear where your line belongs.
The guest keeps the space they chose. The song can reach it.
Last verse! Everyone who brought a name, sing it with me!
Two hundred voices, off-key and loud. Somewhere, a bell rang, and nobody stopped singing.
The bell cannot count a square this loud. For one night, it is losing.
The verse ends before the square decides to become quiet.
They kept the long name in time.
Mostly.
Mostly is a generous place to meet.
Nobody spilled a bowl when they stood up.
That is not solely the table's achievement.
You may share the credit with the soup.
For a moment Mahmut looks at the empty bowls instead of the road out.
We should help put these away.
After you have finished sitting down.
One last useful thing. A conversation nobody has to carry.
You make everything sound like work.
Only the enjoyable work.
It did not move once.
The pad fits.
Someone sat in the middle instead of hiding it at the end.
That was the useful part.
Jori turns the chair to face the table again.
Leave it here. Somebody will need it tomorrow.
The helper found the storehouse without calling you.
Good. They remembered the turn.
And you got to sit down.
I thought I would be checking the turn all evening.
She starts to rise for the next load, then sees the helper already teaching someone else the route.
Tomorrow I may draw a very good route to breakfast.
Are you keeping the wrong notes?
They were somebody's way of getting into the song.
Mine was particularly inventive.
I have made a respectful note of it.
Pippa folds the sheet with the corrections still visible.
I will not make it tidier than the evening was.
The bowls go back in stacks. The chairs go back one at a time, except the repaired one.
That one can stay.
It will need a dry place if it rains.
There is a very good way to the storehouse.
And there is room left on the next sheet.
I may revise my contribution.
A table for everyone. A pot for the very brave.
Come on. Before she explains the recipe.
They leave a clear space between the tables. It will be useful when someone arrives tomorrow.
